slides.title: Seven gears for the clock
slides.text: The Great Clock stands silent above the Towers. Its seven gears wait on the workbench, one from each tower. To set a gear in place, you solve that tower's problem, and every problem takes more than one step.

slides.title: A chain of small steps
slides.text: The cold store is at −6°C. It warms 2.5° an hour for 4 hours, then cools 3°. First the warming: 4 × 2.5 = 10, so −6 + 10 = 4. Then the cooling: 4 − 3 = 1°C.

visual.label: The cold store warms, then cools

focus.cue: It starts at −6°C and warms by 4 × 2.5 = 10 degrees.
It ends at 1°C, just above zero.

slides.title: Estimate first, then check
slides.text: Before you work it out, guess roughly. A lantern burns 6 mL of oil in 4 hours. How much does it burn in 10 hours? A good estimate catches a slip.
steps: Estimate: 10 hours is a bit more than 2 × 4
So a bit more than 2 × 6 = 12 mL
15 is a bit more than 12: it makes sense

slides.title: A ladder to the clock face
slides.text: The clock face is 8 meters up the tower wall, and the ladder's foot stands 6 meters out. The ladder is the long side: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, and √100 = 10. The ladder is 10 meters long.

visual.label: The wall, the ground and the ladder

focus.cue: The wall: 8 meters up to the clock face.
The ladder is the long side, across from the square corner.

slides.title: Compare with the right amount
slides.text: A survey map says a path is 48 meters, but it is really 60 meters. The error is 60 − 48 = 12 meters. Percent error compares the error with the real length: 12 ÷ 60 = 0.2, which is 20%.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for the last climb.

words.means: a problem you solve in more than one step, each step using the answer before it
a rough answer worked out first, to check that the exact answer makes sense
how much for one unit, such as 1.5 milliliters of oil in one hour
the error divided by the real amount, written as a percent

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Launch Lab at The Great Clock. Set seven gears, one from each tower: a rate, a change below zero, an equation, a percent error, a slope, a ladder and a missing landing.
slides.alt: Launch Lab on a phone: the Great Clock's first gear, a double number line of hours and milliliters, and a stepper to set the oil for 10 hours.
